title: 8-K exhibit ex991sunandsuncdelistnysel.htm (filed 2026-09-10)
analysis:
## Key Takeaways

- **No operational or financial disclosures**: This 8-K exhibit is exclusively an administrative announcement regarding a stock exchange listing transfer (NYSE → Texas Stock Exchange), effective October 5, 2026. It contains no data on throughput, utilization, capture rates, margins, or guidance.

- **No renewable fuels or RIN/LCFS content**: The filing does not address renewable diesel, SAF economics, capacity, or RIN/LCFS exposure in any capacity.

- **No capital allocation signals**: There is no mention of capex, distributions, buybacks, or balance sheet actions tied to this transfer.

- **Business description reiterated (unchanged)**: The filing repeats standard descriptive figures — ~14,000 miles of pipeline, 170+ terminals, >15 billion gallons distributed annually, ~11,000 retail locations across 33 countries/territories — but these are boilerplate "About Sunoco" figures, not new operational metrics or guidance updates.

- **Corporate/ticker mechanics only**: SUN and SUNC will retain identical ticker symbols on TXSE; no unitholder action is required, and the transfer is framed as aligning with SUN/SUNC's Texas-based operational footprint.

## Market Signal

This filing is not fuels-market-relevant news: it signals only an exchange-listing/venue change for SUN and SUNC's common units, and refined-products traders should not draw any inference about throughput, margins, or renewable fuels economics from it.

title: 8-K exhibit tm2625060d1_ex99-1.htm (filed 2026-09-11)
analysis:
## Fuel-Segment Extract: Kroger 2Q26 (period ended Aug 15, 2026)

- **No fuel gallon volumes, fuel comps, or station count data disclosed** in this release — all identical sales metrics (0.2% Q2, 3.4% prior year) are reported *excluding* fuel.
- **Fuel cited as a margin mix headwind**: overall gross margin declined to 22.4% (from 22.5%) partly due to "the mix effect of higher fuel sales" alongside higher shrink and transportation costs.
- **Fuel called out as an EPS tailwind**: CFO David Kennerley attributed adjusted EPS growth (+5%) in part to "strong pharmacy and fuel performance," alongside cost savings and eCommerce profitability gains — but no margin rate or dollar figure was quantified.
- **Total sales including fuel rose to $34.6B from $33.9B**, while sales excluding fuel (and adjusting for Vitacost sale/fulfillment center exits) grew just 0.1%, implying fuel sales dollars were a meaningful contributor to the topline increase, though volume/price split is not broken out.
- No commentary on membership-fuel programs, fuel center openings/closures, or fuel-specific capital allocation.

**Signal for fuels markets:** Kroger's fuel business appears to have benefited from higher fuel sales dollars (likely price-driven given no volume disclosure) and contributed positively to profitability, but the company provides no granular fuel margin, gallon, or station data — limiting this release's utility as a fuels-market indicator beyond confirming fuel remained a net-positive, low-margin-mix drag on retail gross margin.

title: 8-K exhibit exhibit991-investorprese.htm (filed 2026-09-08)
analysis:
# CVR Energy (CVI) — Refined Fuels Takeaways from Sept 2026 Investor Presentation

- **Throughput/utilization**: Total nameplate crude capacity 206,500 bpd (Coffeyville 132,000 bpd + Wynnewood 74,500 bpd, complexity 10.8); TTM throughputs ~215,000 bpd with 97% liquid volume yield and 92% gasoline/distillate yield. Five-year average utilization is 90% (incl. turnarounds); **no planned Petroleum Segment turnarounds in 2026** (next ones: Wynnewood 2027, Coffeyville 2028), implying sustained high run rates through year-end.

- **Crack spreads improved sharply but capture rates fell**: Group 3 2-1-1 crack averaged **$33.34/bbl in 1H26 vs. $20.89/bbl in 1H25**, yet CVR's adjusted margin capture dropped to **26% in 1H26 from 46% in FY25**, driven by higher RIN prices, realized derivative losses, and steeper crude backwardation — margin capture, not crack spreads, is the bottleneck.

- **RIN/SRE exposure remains material**: Company is "diligently pursuing" Small Refinery Exemptions at Wynnewood; SREs granted in Aug 2025 and Aug 2026 would have added ~6% to average margin capture over 2021–2025, underscoring how RFS compliance costs are a persistent drag on realized margins.

title: 10-Q (filed 2026-09-08)
analysis:
## Casey's General Stores (CASY) — Q1 FY2027 10-Q: Refined Fuels Takeaways

- **Fuel volume/throughput:** Gallons sold rose 2.5% YoY to 934.2M (from 911.8M), though same-store gallons *declined* 0.3% — growth came entirely from net new stores (64 more locations, incl. 12 acquisitions), not underlying demand strength.

- **Margin capture — historically elevated:** Fuel margin (revenue less COGS ex-D&A) was 47.8 cents/gallon vs. 41.0 cents/gallon a year ago, despite the *percentage* margin compressing to 12.0% of fuel revenue (from 13.7%) as retail price/gallon jumped 33.0%. Management explicitly flags this as "historically higher than average" for the company and industry, cautioning it can swing unpredictably.

- **RIN exposure quantified:** Recognized $25.7M from 10.9M RINs monetized in Q1 FY27 vs. $6.7M from 6.1M RINs a year earlier — RIN volume/value nearly doubled/quadrupled, but net impact to fuel margin was described as "minimal" since higher RIN revenue was offset by higher RIN-related costs. Company early-adopted ASU 2026-02 (environmental credits), now marking RINs to fair value (Level 1) as noncompliance environmental credits; balances remain immaterial to the balance sheet.

- **Wholesale/logistics footprint:** Wholesale fuel activity comprises ~3% of total revenue; Casey's self-distributes the majority of its fuel via its own Waco, TX terminal and continues hedging bulk inventoried fuel (pipeline/terminal) with futures — derivative positions remain immaterial as of quarter-end.

- **EV build-out still marginal:** Only 294 charging ports across 68 of 2,959 stores (14 of 19 states) — company reiterates Midwest EV demand lags coastal markets, signaling no near-term cannibalization risk to gasoline/diesel volumes.

- **Capital allocation tilts toward fuel infrastructure/growth:** Capex jumped to $194.4M (from $110.0M) and acquisition spend to $43.9M (from $9.5M) alongside a share buyback program expansion from $400M to $1.0B (Board authorized June 2026), signaling confidence in continued fuel-retail footprint growth even amid normalizing margins.

**Signal for fuels markets:** Casey's results reflect a retail fuel margin environment that remains unusually rich (47.8¢/gal) even as percentage spreads compress with rising pump prices, while RIN monetization is scaling in volume

title: 8-K exhibit q1fy2027earningspressrelea.htm (filed 2026-09-08)
analysis:
## Key Takeaways — Casey's General Stores Q1 FY2027 (Fuel-Relevant Metrics)

- **Fuel margin expansion drove profit growth**: Fuel margin (excluding credit card fees) rose to **47.8¢/gallon** from **41.0¢/gallon** YoY (+16.6%), pushing total fuel gross profit up **19.6%** to **$446.9 million** despite roughly flat volumes — indicating retail fuel capture/spread strength outpaced volume growth this quarter.

- **Same-store fuel demand softened**: Same-store gallons sold declined **0.3%** YoY (vs. +1.7% in the prior-year quarter), though positive on a two-year stack (+1.4%). Total fuel gallons sold still grew **2.5%** to **934.2 million gallons**, driven entirely by net store count growth (64 more stores YoY, including the Fikes acquisition), not underlying demand.

- **No renewable diesel/SAF or RIN/LCFS exposure disclosed**: As a fuel retailer (not a refiner or producer), Casey's has no stated renewable fuel production capacity, RIN generation/obligation, or LCFS credit exposure in this release — fuel economics here reflect retail marketing spread only, not refining/blending economics.

- **Guidance unchanged**: FY2027 outlook reaffirmed — same-store fuel gallons expected in a **-1% to +1%** range, consistent with the current quarter's softness; management flagged no shift due to macro fuel demand trends.

- **Capital allocation favors expansion over fuel infrastructure specifics**: Store count grew to **2,959** (net +15 in-quarter, including 12 acquired sites), with capex guidance of **~$800 million** for FY2027 and continued M&A-driven growth (target **120+ new stores**), suggesting continued investment in fuel-dispensing retail footprint amid integration of the Fikes acquisition (ahead of schedule per CEO commentary).

- **Liquidity/returns steady**: $1.4B available liquidity ($524M cash), $45.6M in buybacks this quarter, $973M remaining authorization, and a raised-looking but flat $0.65/share dividend — signaling no acute capital strain tied to fuel margin volatility.

**Market signal**: Casey's results show retail fuel marketing margins remain historically elevated even as underlying same-store gasoline demand is flat-to-slightly-negative, reinforcing that convenience-fuel retailers are capturing wider spreads in a volatile wholesale fuel environment rather than benefiting from volume growth — a dynamic more reflective of retail margin resilience than refined product demand strength.

title: 10-Q (filed 2026-08-28)
analysis:
## Fuel-Segment Extract — Walmart Inc. (WMT) 10-Q, Q2 FY2027 (period ended July 31, 2026)

- **Sam's Club U.S. fuel sales surged**: "Fuel and other" category net sales rose to $4,192M (Q2) from $3,064M YoY (+37%), and $7,635M (6mo) from $5,915M YoY (+29%), reflecting **higher fuel prices and volumes**.
- **Fuel-driven comp-sales boost**: Higher fuel sales added **+4.2 pts** to Sam's Club U.S. comparable sales in Q2 (vs. a *drag* of -2.6 pts in the prior-year quarter) and **+3.2 pts** for the six-month period (vs. -2.6 pts prior year) — a swing of roughly 680–580 bps YoY in fuel's comp contribution.
- **Fuel-related cost scale**: Total fuel-related cost of sales and opex for Sam's Club U.S. was **$3.4B** (Q2) and **$6.1B** (6mo), up from $2.3B and $4.5B YoY, respectively — confirming fuel volume/price growth flowed through both revenue and cost lines.
- **Ex-fuel vs. including-fuel divergence**: Sam's Club U.S. net sales growth excluding fuel was only **+4.5%** (Q2) vs. **+8.8%** including fuel, and **+4.2%** vs **+7.5%** for six months — fuel accounted for roughly half of headline growth.
- **Opex leverage from fuel**: Management attributed part of the **26 bps (Q2) / 13 bps (6mo)** decrease in Sam's Club U.S. operating expenses as a % of net sales to "higher fuel sales" (fuel's low opex-intensity dilutes the ratio), partially offset by tech investment and insurance claims costs.

title: 10-Q (filed 2026-08-25)
analysis:
## Fuel-Segment Extract: BJ's Wholesale Club 10-Q (Q2 FY2026, period ended Aug 1, 2026)

- **Station count:** 206 gas stations across 22 states as of August 1, 2026 (down from BJ's operating alongside 267 clubs; company had 255 clubs a year ago, implying net club growth but gas station count not broken out historically in this filing).
- **Gasoline sales mix rising sharply:** "Gasoline and Other" grew to **25% of net sales in Q2 FY26** (vs. 18% in Q2 FY25) and **23% for the 26-week period** (vs. 18% prior year) — the largest categorical mix shift in the disclosure.
- **Gasoline comparable sales:** **+8.8%** for the thirteen weeks and **+6.9%** for the twenty-six weeks ended Aug 1, 2026, driven by both **higher average retail price-per-gallon** and **increased comparable gallons sold** — no absolute gallon figures disclosed.
- **Margin strategy:** Company states it "generally attempt[s] to maintain a fairly stable gross profit per gallon on an absolute dollar basis," so rising retail pump prices lift net sales dollars but are framed as largely margin-neutral per-gallon; volatile crude/wholesale swings cause temporary "margin contraction or expansion" versus competitors depending on procurement timing.
- **Membership-fuel linkage/rewards economics:** Club+ members get a **5¢/gallon** discount at BJ's Gas; BJ's One/One+ co-branded Mastercard holders get up to a **15¢/gallon** discount when paying at BJ's gas locations — reinforcing fuel as a membership-retention lever tied to card royalty/rewards revenue (recognized via royalty revenue and co-brand deferred revenue balances in Note 3).
- **Cost structure:** "Other segment expenses" (which include gasoline cost of revenue) rose from $911.5M to $1.43B YoY in the quarter and from $1.79B to $2.61B YoY for the half, consistent with higher wholesale fuel costs flowing through cost of sales alongside higher retail pump prices.

**Signal for fuels markets:** BJ's data point to firmer retail pump prices and higher fuel volumes through mid-2026 versus the prior-year period, with the retailer maintaining stable per-gallon dollar margins — indicating resilient consumer fuel demand at warehouse-club price points rather than a margin-driven earnings story.

title: Q2 2026 Earnings Release (8-K, filed 2026-07-31)
analysis:
- **Downstream earnings exploded to $4.9B** ($2.4B US + $2.5B international) vs $737M a year ago — the margin capture behind this summer's record crack spreads, on total earnings of $12.1B (21% ROCE, Brent averaging $104).
- **US refineries ran flat-out**: record crude unit throughput of 1.07 MMbpd at >97% utilization — yet US refined product sales fell 4% on weaker gasoline demand. This is a margin story, not a volume story.
- **The Middle East conflict is visibly cutting international product supply**: international refinery inputs down 10%, product sales down 13% on supply disruptions.
- **Retreating from Asian downstream**: sold Hong Kong fuels business; agreed to sell its 50% of Singapore Refining Company plus downstream assets across Vietnam, Australia, Indonesia, the Philippines, and Malaysia (closing 2027).
- Record $8.4B debt paydown in the quarter; $3B structural cost target hit six months early; Hess synergies at $1.5B run-rate.

**Signal for fuels markets**: a major running US refining at physical limits into record margins while shedding international downstream — more evidence that usable product supply, not crude, is the binding constraint.

title: Q2 2026 Earnings Release (8-K, filed 2026-07-31)
analysis:
- **Energy Products (refining) adjusted earnings hit $4.1B for the quarter** — first-half 2026 at $6.9B vs $2.2B in all of 1H 2025, a tripling driven by product margins.
- **Record second-quarter diesel production** (best in their data back to 2014) on strong US Gulf Coast utilization — the industry's max-distillate shift, quantified.
- Product placement flexed around the Middle East disruptions ($900M of YTD earnings impacts, plus an $884M non-US Energy Products impairment); energy products sales rose to 5.7 MMbpd.
- Total: $14.5B GAAP / $14.7B adjusted earnings, $17.2B free cash flow, $9.4B returned to shareholders in the quarter.
- **Corporate note**: completed its redomiciliation July 1 — ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (Texas) replaced the New Jersey parent; same ticker, new SEC registrant.

**Signal for fuels markets**: the largest US refiner by complexity is running record diesel output into a supply-constrained market and still can't soften cracks — confirmation of how tight distillate supply actually is.

title: Q2 2026 Earnings Release (8-K, filed 2026-08-07)
analysis:
- **Fuel margin expansion all the way downstream**: gasoline distribution product margin jumped to $175.0M from $137.9M on higher cents-per-gallon margins — distributors are capturing spread, not just passing through higher prices.
- Adjusted EBITDA +51% to $148.2M; net income nearly tripled to $71.0M; distributable cash flow up 78% to $92.6M.
- Wholesale gasoline/blendstocks margin rose to $78.4M (from $58.8M) on favorable gasoline conditions; distillates/residual margin slipped to $28.1M; bunkering strengthened.
- Total sales of $6.8B vs $4.6B — almost entirely price-driven, mirroring the commodity move.
- Station operations margin flat (~$70M) — the c-store side is steady while the fuel side swings.

**Signal for fuels markets**: price volatility is profit for the distribution layer — Northeast rack-to-retail spreads are wide, and the margin expansion GLP shows suggests pump prices have room to keep rising even if wholesale stabilizes.

title: Q3 FY2026 Earnings Release (8-K, filed 2026-05-28)
analysis:
- **Gasoline was a major comp driver**: US comparable sales rose 9.4% reported but only 6.8% excluding gas prices and FX — fuel-price inflation contributed roughly 2.6 points, one of the largest gas contributions to comps in years (quarter ended May 10, before the summer spike accelerated).
- Fiscal Q3 (12 weeks): net sales $69.2B (+11.6%), net income $2.19B ($4.93/share); 931 warehouses, 639 in the US.
- The release gives no gallon or fuel-margin detail (Costco reserves that for the earnings call) — but the reported-vs-adjusted comp gap is the cleanest public marker of member fuel spending.
- Membership fees +10.7% to $1.37B — the model that lets Costco run fuel at thin margins as a traffic driver is compounding.

**Signal for fuels markets**: high-volume discount retail is passing higher fuel prices straight into reported sales while using cheap gas as a membership draw — expect Costco to stay the price floor in its markets. Fiscal Q4 (report due late September) will capture the full summer price surge.

title: Investor Presentation — April 2026
analysis:
- **Benicia is out**: buried in a slide-34 footnote — the Benicia refinery's processing units were idled in April 2026, leaving Wilmington (85 kbpd crude) as Valero's only California refinery. Portfolio now stands at 14 refineries, 3.0 MMbpd throughput / 2.5 MMbpd crude capacity, 61% concentrated on the Gulf Coast.
- **SAF is live at scale**: DGD Port Arthur SAF project (completed 4Q24) can upgrade up to 235M gal/yr — half the plant's renewable diesel output — to SAF for $315M total cost, expected to clear the 25% after-tax IRR hurdle. Total DGD platform: 1.22B gal/yr.
- **Renewable diesel is self-funded and best-in-class**: DGD cumulative EBITDA of $3,005M (VLO share) now exceeds cumulative capex of $2,071M. 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $0.59/gal led all RD peers ($0.21 peer average; some peers negative) — though well below the $2+/gal LCFS-era peaks of 2021–22.
- **Refining discipline over growth**: no new capacity — capital goes to optimization (St. Charles FCC project, $230M, 2H26 completion, +15 kbpd resid processing and +6 kbpd alkylate) at a 25% IRR hurdle. Lowest cash opex/bbl vs PSX/MPC/DINO/PBF; 2025 was their best-ever year for safety and mechanical availability.
- **Cash returned, not reinvested in barrels**: $4.0B returned in 2025 (67% payout), share count down 46% since 2012, dividend at $4.80 annualized for 2026, ~$1.4B sustaining capex.
- **Export lean**: >1.5 MMbpd ratable wholesale supply (>50% of light products), 349 kbpd exports in 2025, with Latin America taking 75% of US product exports as regional refining runs decline.

**Signal for fuels markets**: America's largest independent refiner is shrinking West Coast supply, capping domestic capacity growth in favor of buybacks, and steering its renewables platform toward mandated SAF markets — a structurally tightening posture for US refined product supply, especially California gasoline and diesel/jet.
